environment.concurrentWorkloads: No build or other benchmark started by this harness; other host activity is not controlled.

webView.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/155.0.0.0

method.workload: Actual production store.trigger(status), one demo profile, no running tasks; production callback must return an idle status object.
method.scope: WebView JavaScript before trigger to production callback entry; includes request preparation, selected carrier, Rust/WebView bridge where applicable, Python handler, JSON and encrypted SecureWebSocket for WebSocket. Excludes CDP round trips, transport restart, game, screenshot and rendering.
method.quantile: Zero-based sorted index floor(n*p), capped at n-1; successful samples only; failed attempts retained separately; no outlier removal or forced GC.
method.blockMean: Elapsed time for 50 consecutive calls divided by successful calls; includes callback validation and loop overhead. A block with failures has no block mean.
method.readiness: From calling setTransportMode to authenticated and all data initialized. Includes stopping the previous mode, process restart, authentication and sync with warm OS caches; not cold application startup.
method.inference: Single host/session; six order-balanced blocks per mode, no confidence interval or universal speedup claim. Timer-quantized individual samples must not be used for zero-denominator speedup ratios.
method.outputEquivalence: Every production callback is exactly 44 UTF-8 JSON bytes after the store removes the transport envelope/timestamp: command=status, status=ok, data={}. This is not encrypted wire size or a large-payload throughput workload.
method.network: Frontend and backend on the same host; WebSocket uses loopback. No LAN/WAN network path.
